question: A 40-year-old woman undergoes emergency surgery for a perforated sigmoid diverticulitis with faecal contamination of the peritoneum. According to the surgical wound classification system, this wound is:

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Clean wounds are uninfected, non-traumatic, with no break in aseptic technique and no entry into viscera.
Clean-contaminated wounds involve a controlled entry into the alimentary, respiratory or genitourinary tract without unusual contamination.
Contaminated wounds include gross spillage from the gastrointestinal tract; faecal peritonitis is more severe, constituting Class IV.
Correct. Class IV (dirty/infected) includes wounds with perforated viscera and established infection or faecal peritonitis — exactly the scenario here. Infection is assumed to be already present.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the four-class CDC wound classification: Clean (I), Clean-contaminated (II), Contaminated (III), Dirty/Infected (IV).
Well done. Faecal peritonitis from perforated diverticulitis constitutes a Class IV (dirty/infected) wound with the highest risk of postoperative surgical site infection.
